steps.title: Attribute the finding
steps.evidence: Record the public location, issuer, environment, stable credential identifier and the evidence connecting it to a service. Keep the credential value out of the incident record.

steps.title: Choose containment and cutover
steps.evidence: Identify the issuer administrator and dependent workloads. An active compromise may call for immediate revocation and a service interruption. If a controlled overlap is appropriate, agree who ends it and by when.

steps.title: Replace or retire the access
steps.evidence: Capture the issuer’s change or expiry event. Where a replacement is needed, deliver it to each consumer and verify normal application behavior. A vault version change by itself leaves the issuer state open.

steps.title: Reconcile old access and investigate use
steps.evidence: Check the old credential’s status at the issuer. Record what the target logs cover, the exposure window reviewed and any observed activity. Track sessions or tokens already issued separately where applicable.

steps.title: Close with evidence
steps.evidence: Record issuer invalidation, consumer cutover or retirement, and the outcome of the usage review. If the available logs leave impact unknown, record that uncertainty separately from containment.

cases.title: A payment API key appears in a personal repository
cases.owners: AppSec can identify the repository. The payments team owns the integration, and a Stripe administrator controls the key. The developer who published it may have neither responsibility.
cases.cutover: If an overlap is used, move the payment service to the replacement and verify normal requests. Check the old key’s expiry in the correct Stripe account and environment. Review the available request history for the exposure window.
cases.miss: The repository is private again, but the old API key is still valid.
cases.close: Issuer expiry time, successful payment-service cutover and the scope and outcome of the target log review.

cases.title: A shared database password is rotated
cases.owners: The database team controls the login. The vault owner manages the stored value. An API and an overnight batch job both consume it.
cases.cutover: Confirm how the selected provider handles overlap. Watch both consumers adopt the replacement, including the next batch run. Check existing database sessions separately and have the database owner review authentication records.
cases.miss: The API looks healthy while the overnight job still holds the retired password.
cases.close: Target-side credential change, current access state, application and batch-job evidence, and the database audit window.

cases.title: A release pipeline moves from a stored key to federation
cases.owners: The build team owns the pipeline. Cloud IAM owns the trust relationship and the long-lived credential that previously authorized releases.
cases.cutover: Verify the intended workflow can deploy with temporary credentials and a different test workflow is denied. Retire the old cloud key at the issuer, then review its usage and any previously issued sessions within available log coverage.
cases.miss: The pipeline now uses federation, but a copied long-lived cloud key still works.
cases.close: Successful federated release, a narrowly scoped trust policy, old-key retirement evidence and a documented cloud log review.
